items.title: Aebersold Jamey — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: On the Woody Shaw, Volume 9 there, that you’re looking at, we recorded it here in the basement.

ctx.x: It was just a scratch track, or at least they were going to...

Right. On the Woody Shaw, Volume 9 there, that you’re looking at, we recorded it here in the basement. He was over in one little room here, with headphones on, and he was soloing. I’ve actually got that on the half-inch tape back in the back, and some day I need to send it off to somebody and have them bake it, just to hear what he played while they were comping.

The lineup... One of those things, too, as a musician, being able to hear these guys perform or play together, even if they’re laying just a foundation for you as a learning tool... That chemistry, the playing, it’s something that... It’s inspiring.

items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: I just happened to have a cassette of J.J. Johnson with Horace Silver and Woody Show and Joe Henderson in my — and I had a cassette player back then and I had that cassette.

ctx.x: Let me ask you, I’m sorry, go ahead.

That reminds me of a story. I was doing a clinic up at Youngstown, Ohio, probably thirty years ago, and I had some students playing the scales up to the ninth and back down and chords, and we may have played a blues or something. But it was rudimentary exercises. And I was packing up to leave ‘cause a guy was going to drive me back to Pittsburgh in order to fly back to Louisville and do this all in one day. And a gentleman walks up to me, he looked like he was about 33 years old, and he plays the trombone. He…
